See also: porcelaną

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From porcelano (“porcelain”, noun) +‎ -a.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /port͡seˈlana/
  • Rhymes: -ana
  • Syllabification: por‧ce‧la‧na

Adjective

[edit]

porcelana (accusative singular porcelanan, plural porcelanaj, accusative plural porcelanajn)

  1. made of or relating to, porcelain
    porcelana statueto ― a porcelain statuette

Polish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • porcénal (Chełmno-Dobrzyń)
  • porcynela (Far Masovian)

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin porcellāna.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔr.t͡sɛˈla.na/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ana
  • Syllabification: por‧ce‧la‧na

Noun

[edit]

porcelana f (related adjective porcelanowy)

  1. porcelain

Declension

[edit]
Declension of porcelana
singular
nominative porcelana
genitive porcelany
dative porcelanie
accusative porcelanę
instrumental porcelaną
locative porcelanie
vocative porcelano

Derived terms

[edit]
adverbs
  • jak słoń w składzie porcelany

[edit]

Spanish

Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
porcelana
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Late Latin porcella
Old Italian porcella
Old Italian -ana
Old Italian porcellanabor.
Spanish porcelana

    Inherited from Old Spanish porcelana, from Old Italian porcellana (“cowrie; chinaware”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /poɾθeˈlana/ [poɾ.θeˈla.na] (Spain, Equatorial Guinea)
    • IPA(key): /poɾseˈlana/ [poɾ.seˈla.na] (Latin America, Philippines)
    • Rhymes: -ana
    • Syllabification: por‧ce‧la‧na

    Noun

    [edit]

    porcelana f (plural porcelanas)

    1. porcelain
